title: The parents' group treasurer
scenario:
Elena is the volunteer treasurer of a school parents' group. This month there are four jobs:

1. Send a friendly reminder about the yearly fee to 120 families.
2. Turn the school's new 12-page trip policy into 5 short points for parents.
3. Decide which families get the fee waived this year.
4. Answer a parent who asks if the group must pay tax on money from the summer fair.

Elena has a chat app and asks you which parts to give it.

questions.prompt: Which job is the best one to hand off (the app drafts, Elena checks and sends)?

options.text: Job 1, the fee reminder, because it is a draft Elena can read and fix.
options.explanation: Right. Drafting is what chat apps do well, and Elena can check every line before it goes out. It is a hand-off with a person at the end.

options.text: Job 3, the fee waivers, because the app can be fair to every family.
options.explanation: This is a decision about real families, and Elena's group owns it. The ChatGPT docs say AI should support judgment, not replace it.

options.text: Job 4, the tax question, because the app knows the rules of every country.
options.explanation: Tax is a financial and legal question. The ChatGPT docs say these decisions need expert review, and answers can be wrong while they look right.

options.text: None of them, because a chat app is not safe for any work in a school.
options.explanation: Too strict. Some parts are low-risk and easy to check, like a friendly reminder. Keep is one answer, not the only one.

questions.prompt: For job 2, the 12-page trip policy, what is the safe way to split the work?

options.text: Ask the app for 5 points and send them, because summaries are what it does best.
options.explanation: Summaries are a good fit, but a point can be wrong or missing. A person must check before parents read it.

options.text: Write all 5 points by hand, because a summary of a policy is always high-stakes.
options.explanation: Too strict. This is a good hand-off when someone checks it against the policy.

options.text: Let the app draft 5 points, then check each one against the 12 pages before sending.
options.explanation: Right. The OpenAI docs recommend a human review before outputs are used, and say the reviewer needs the original material. Elena has the 12 pages to check against.

options.text: Ask the app if its own summary is correct, and send it if the app says yes.
options.explanation: The OpenAI docs ask for a human review by someone who has the original material. The app saying yes to its own summary is not that review.

questions.prompt: For job 3, the fee waivers, how can the app help without taking the decision?

options.text: Give it the list of families and let it choose who gets a waiver this year.
options.explanation: That hands the decision to the app. A decision about people stays with Elena and the group.

options.text: Ask it for questions the group could use to set fair rules, then the group decides.
options.explanation: Right. This is a share: the app helps the group think, and people make the decision. It supports judgment and does not replace it.

options.text: Ask it which families seem poorest from their names and addresses.
options.explanation: The app would judge real families on guesses, not on facts, and it still takes the decision. The decision stays with the group.

options.text: Keep the app out of it, so it gives no help at all this year.
options.explanation: Keeping it is allowed, but the question asks how the app can help. A share lets it help the group think while people still decide.

questions.prompt: For job 4, the tax question, what should Elena do?

options.text: Ask the app, and if the answer sounds sure, send it on to the parent.
options.explanation: A sure tone is not proof. Answers can look correct and be very mistaken, and tax is a high-stakes area.

options.text: Tell the parent the group never pays tax, because it is only a volunteer group.
options.explanation: That is a guess, not a checked answer. Tax rules depend on the place and the group.

options.text: Ask two different chat apps and send the answer if both of them agree.
options.explanation: Two apps agreeing is still not expert review. The ChatGPT docs say financial and legal decisions need appropriate expert review.

options.text: Keep it: ask an accountant or the tax office, and use the app only to word the question.
options.explanation: Right. Financial and legal questions need an expert. The Gemini Apps Help says not to rely on its answers for professional advice. The app can still help Elena write a clear question.
